facts.statement: Phosphatosaurus was named in 1955 and is a monotypic genus with the type species P. gavialoides.
facts.quote: Named in 1955, Phosphatosaurus is a monotypic genus; the type species is P. gavialoides.

facts.statement: Phosphatosaurus lived during the early Eocene and its fossils have been found in Tunisia and Mali.
facts.quote: It existed during the early Eocene, with fossils having been found from North Africa in Tunisia and Mali.

facts.statement: Phosphatosaurus was a large dyrosaurid with a skull longer than 1 meter and blunt teeth.
facts.quote: Phosphatosaurus is a large dyrosaurid (skull of more than 1 m in length) with blunt teeth.

facts.statement: The tip of Phosphatosaurus's snout was spoon-shaped due to a lateral expansion of the rostral part of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: The tip of the snout is spoon-shaped from a lateral expansion of the rostral portion of the mandible.

facts.statement: Phosphatosaurus had nonhomodont dentition featuring unique paired tooth sockets in the lower jaw where the sockets were closer together than adjacent ones.
facts.quote: The dentition is nonhomodont. Alveolar "couplets" are present in the lower jaw of Phosphatosaurus in which paired tooth sockets, or alveoli, are closer to one another than to the alveoli next to them.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the gaps between the paired tooth sockets in the lower jaw may have accommodated larger upper teeth.
facts.quote: It is possible that the diastemata between the couplets served to receive larger maxillary teeth.

facts.statement: Eric Buffetaut assigned Phosphatosaurus to the subfamily Phosphatosaurinae in 1979, defining it as a clade with Sokotosaurus.
facts.quote: Phosphatosaurus was assigned in 1979 to the newly named subfamily Phosphatosaurinae by Eric Buffetaut, who considered the subfamily to be the clade formed by Phosphatosaurus and the closely related Sokotosaurus.

facts.statement: Recent studies have tentatively questioned the validity of the Phosphatosaurinae subfamily due to limited anatomical knowledge of the genera involved.
facts.quote: However, other authors of more recent studies have been tentative in considering the taxon valid because there is currently little knowledge of the anatomy of either genus.

facts.statement: Phosphatosaurus is classified as a basal dyrosaurid and is frequently placed near the base of dyrosaurid phylogenetic trees.
facts.quote: Phosphatosaurus is considered to be a basal dyrosaurid, and is often positioned near the base of phylogenetic trees of dyrosaurids.

facts.statement: Most phylogenetic analyses show Phosphatosaurus and Sokotosuchus forming a clade that is more closely related to each other than to any other dyrosaurid genus.
facts.quote: In most analyses, Phosphatosaurus and Sokotosuchus form a clade. These two genera are more closely related to one another than to any other genus of dyrosaurid.

facts.statement: The time range for Phosphatosaurus spans from the Campanian to the Ypresian, approximately 83.6 to 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Ypresian (83.6 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: The close relationship between Phosphatosaurus and the Cretaceous genus Sokotosuchus implies a long ghost lineage extending back to the Maastrichtian that lacks fossil evidence.
facts.quote: Because Phosphatosaurus is only known from Paleogene localities, the close relationship with Sokotosuchus implies that there is a long ghost lineage extending back into the Maastrichtian that is not known in the fossil record.

rejected.statement: Recent studies suggest that the short-snouted dyrosaurid Chenanisuchus may be more basal than the clade containing Phosphatosaurus and Sokotosuchus.
rejected.quote: More recent phylogenetic studies have considered Chenanisuchus, a short-snouted dyrosairid named in 2005, to be even more basal than the clade containing Phosphatosaurus and Sokotosuchus.
